requirements.text: Move the mug to the right of the headphones

outcomes.description: Move the mug so that it is positioned to the right of the headphones.

nodes.question: Can the source mug be matched to an edited object from visible identity and continuity cues, and can its displacement or position relative to the headphones be judged?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if visible cues reliably match the source mug to an edited object and permit judging its position relative to the headphones. Fail only if clear evidence establishes the source mug is absent or unchanged and no matching moved mug is present. Unknown if the blue remnant, candidate mugs, or other evidence do not resolve identity or position. Record separately any visible displacement/progress and its basis; do not equate ambiguity with no progress or infer identity from right-side placement.
nodes.binding: Compare the source’s large light-blue handled mug left of the headphones with every edited candidate and the blurred blue form at its former location. Record shape, handle, color, scale, location, and contextual continuity cues that support or undermine each match. Distinguish a plausible but unconfirmed match from a reliable match; do not assume the rightmost mug is the source. Separately report any visible displacement evidence and whether the source mug’s relation to the headphones is judgeable. This is evidence availability, not fulfillment.

nodes.question: Using s1’s identity and continuity observations, is there evidence that the source mug moved toward the right of the headphones, and is its final right-side placement verified?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if s1’s evidence supports a reliable match to the source mug and the edited counterpart is visibly right of the headphones; report the matching cues and final relation. Fail only if the source mug is reliably identified and clear evidence shows it did not move toward the requested position. Unknown if identity or displacement cannot be resolved. If identity is uncertain, separately state whether any visible evidence supports displacement/progress and why it does or does not establish progress of the source mug; do not count another mug’s position as progress. A verified same-mug right-side relation is complete; evidenced movement of that same mug toward the right without reaching it is partial; otherwise do not infer absence from uncertainty.
nodes.binding: Use s1’s recorded comparison of the source mug’s visible attributes and location against the blurred blue remnant and each edited mug. Explicitly cite which continuity cues support or undermine a candidate match, and distinguish plausible from reliable identity. Compare source and edited positions relative to the headphones only for a reliably matched object. Separately assess visible displacement evidence without assuming the rightmost mug is the source.

nodes.question: Is the mug visibly positioned to the right of the headphones?
nodes.criteria: Apply the original rubric to R1 using only the saved support observations. Complete (yes) only if s1 and s2 establish that the source mug itself is identified in the edit and is visibly to the right of the headphones. Partial only if s2 records evidence that this same mug moved toward the requested position but is not yet to the right. Absent (no) only if the observations provide clear evidence that no requested movement progressed. Unknown if source-mug identity, movement, or position is unresolved, or if the observations do not establish progress or absence. A different mug's position, object presence, or unrelated edits cannot establish fulfillment.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

response.content: {"accepted":false,"reason":"The support checks do not preserve the requested relation and extent reliably. s2 treats movement “toward” the right as partial even though the instruction only requests the final relation “to the right”; movement toward it could be in an unrelated direction or leave the mug still left of the headphones. Conversely, s2’s fail condition (“did not move toward”) does not establish that no requested progress occurred, so it cannot support absence. The fulfillment readout inherits this unsupported partial/absent logic. Require evidence of movement toward the right-side relation for partial, and clear evidence of no such progress for absent; otherwise leave unresolved."}
